clue.text: The retiring may find it illuminating, on reflection

definitions.text: The retiring may find it illuminating, on reflection

blocks.clueFragment: The retiring may find it illuminating
blocks.note: surface reading: shy people might find something enlightening
setter's reading: people going to bed are lit by a shaft of reflected light from the night sky

explanation.surface: A reserved person finds something enlightening after some careful thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' means going to bed, not shy, and 'on reflection' is literal: moonlight is sunlight bounced off the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of moonlight shines into a bedroom at night, and the moon only reflects the sun's light.

clue.text: Soldiers once assembled on trains crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning over something, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: people who have assembled have met
the Usk is a river in South Wales
RY is short for railway

explanation.surface: Old-time troops gather on board trains as they cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed after. The Usk flows through South Wales to the Severn estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry can mean a body of musketeers collectively, soldiers armed with muskets in times past.

clue.text: Children's high jump

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's young or descendants
second meaning, read cryptically: a leap launched off the ground, split into two words

explanation.surface: Kids taking part in the high jump at a sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into two words: a spring from a standing start, off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's or animal's children or young, the next generation.

clue.text: Master is anaemic in some degree

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here within the qualification

blocks.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
someone anaemic looks pale or wan

explanation.surface: The boss is somewhat short of iron in the blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some degree' reads as 'to some extent', but 'some degree' is a university qualification holding the pale word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bwana is a Swahili form of address meaning master or sir, used in colonial East Africa.

clue.text: Skill to limit what incorrectly gets across

indicators.note: incorrectly means set out wrongly, so the letters of that word need putting in a new order
to limit something is to bound it on both sides, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Talent sets a boundary on what wrongly gets through.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart is an old or nautical preposition meaning across, from side to side of something.

clue.text: A work originally in French that is obscure

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written
que is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: A piece of writing first published in French proves hard to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' follows the work in the answer, a loose ordering; 'originally in French' tells you to put 'that' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque is hard to see through or understand, so it is an adjective for unclear writing.

clue.text: A suitor's simple argument

blocks.note: plain means simple, unadorned
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A wooer makes a straightforward case for the hand of his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suitor' suggests a would-be lover, but here it is someone who brings a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the person who brings a suit in a court of law, so literally a suitor.

clue.text: Moderately turns tail, being of peaceful disposition

indicators.note: turns tail here means the tail end of the word is turned round, its final pair flipped

blocks.note: quite means moderately, as in quite good

explanation.surface: Someone who backs off from a fight in a mild way is a peaceable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns tail' suggests running away; here only the last two letters are swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet person is calm and gentle by temperament, peaceful in their disposition.

clue.text: Regard for opponents at bridge, sound players

indicators.note: sound tells us the next word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: East and South sit on opposing sides at the bridge table
players make up a team

explanation.surface: Respect for the rival pair at the bridge table, solid players.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South partner against East-West, so East and South are opponents; 'sound' looks like an adjective praising them.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem means regard or respect, as in holding someone in high regard.

clue.text: Fox, for one, cooked about noon

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece surrounds the second

blocks.note: fried is one way food is cooked
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: A fox is fried for lunch at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is not the animal but George Fox, founder of the Quakers, formally the Religious Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers are called Friends, and George Fox founded their society, so he was one.

clue.text: Note introducing a condition rejected in European capital

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these words are read from right to left

blocks.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
'if' introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A diplomatic note setting out a condition is turned down in a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, which makes it a European capital.

clue.text: Basil and Rosemary have a place in his study

definitions.text: Basil and Rosemary have a place in his study

blocks.note: surface reading: two people, perhaps students, who share a study room

blocks.clueFragment: have a place in his study
blocks.note: setter's reading: basil and rosemary are culinary and medicinal plants, the subject of a certain expert's study

explanation.surface: Two people called Basil and Rosemary have been given room in some man's study.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters make Basil and Rosemary look like people's names; they are plants, and 'study' is a field of learning rather than a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist studies and uses plants such as basil and rosemary for medicine or cookery.

clue.text: Sickly pal needs a walk by the sea

indicators.note: something sickly is out of sorts, so the following letters are in poor shape and must be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: An unwell friend is advised to take a stroll along the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, typically along a seafront, where people stroll.

clue.text: Northern soldiers including it as constituent of gunpowder

indicators.note: including means holding something inside, so the next word sits within the soldiers

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops from the north count it as an ingredient of gunpowder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre (potassium nitrate), is the oxidising ingredient in black powder alongside charcoal and sulphur.

clue.text: Clothing we hear swimmer intended to put on

indicators.note: we hear says the words that follow are taken by their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: a ray is a flat sea fish
intended means meant

explanation.surface: Someone meant to slip on some clothes, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To put on' simply extends the idea of clothing; 'ray meant' said aloud gives the old word for garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic or literary word for clothing and garments.

clue.text: Men let oil blend into a soothing agent

indicators.note: to blend is to mix together, so the letters get stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Men mix oil into a balm to calm the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a cream or ointment that softens and soothes the skin.

clue.text: Finally shed tear - extremely puny and ineffectual

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the following word
extremely points to the two extreme ends of the following word

blocks.note: the last letter of shed
a rip is a tear in fabric
the first and last letters of puny

explanation.surface: Someone finally sheds a tear, being weedy and feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puny and ineffectual' looks like a two-word definition, but 'puny' is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Drippy is informal for feeble, wet and lacking character, so an ineffectual person can be called drippy.

clue.text: Element briefly found in the borders of Peru

definitions.text: Element briefly found in the borders of Peru

blocks.note: surface reading: some substance was quickly discovered somewhere in South America
setter's reading: the chemical symbol of the element is the outside letters of Peru

explanation.surface: A chemical element is fleetingly detected along the frontiers of a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' means in short form: the element's symbol is Pu, the first and last letters of Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonium is the radioactive element, atomic number 94, whose chemical symbol is Pu.

clue.text: Clothing sailors needed on southern river?

blocks.note: men are ordinary sailors, as opposed to officers
S is short for southern
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: What should sailors wear on a southern river?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the clue reads like a question about dress; the river is in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is the retail term for clothes made for men.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian cutting a metal for Tutankhamun's mask

indicators.note: cutting into something means slicing into the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
Tutankhamun's famous funeral mask is made of gold
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian craftsman works a precious metal for the boy king's mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Egyptian' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Ancient'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, just as ancient things have.

clue.text: Live wire secures rise for large number in party

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means going upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top
secures means holds fast, so the first piece grips the second inside it

blocks.note: a do is a party
many means a large number

explanation.surface: An electrified cable fixed in place for a big crowd at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live wire' looks electrical, but it means an energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a forceful, energetic person, just as a live wire is someone lively and active.

clue.text: Endlessly put up with us tucking in to spread throughout

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off
tucking in means placing something snugly inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to put up with something is to suffer it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates us endlessly, as we settle in and make ourselves at home everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking in' sounds like eating, but it signals that the small word goes inside; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffuse is to spread through or over something, as colour or light fills a scene.

clue.text: Diabolical contributor to displays at an ice-rink

indicators.note: a contributor to something is a part of it, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, starting near the end of displays

explanation.surface: Someone devilish helps put on shows at a skating rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means of or like Satan, the devil, so it is a synonym for diabolical.

clue.text: Vacillate in policy, making various points about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the first set of letters is wrapped round the second

blocks.note: several compass points: south, east, east and west
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A government flip-flops, steering in several directions over an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old convention; the compass points wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to swing back and forth between positions, which is what vacillating over policy means.

clue.text: Support beheading treacherous person

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the first letter of the following word goes

blocks.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: Backing an execution of a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden frame that holds up a painting or blackboard, so it is a support.

clue.text: Be sparing -- remove cream from top of pinta

indicators.note: top of, in a down clue, points to the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: to skim milk is to take the cream off it
the first letter of pinta

explanation.surface: Economise by taking the cream off the top of the milk.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, from an old advertising slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy or sparing, using less than is needed.

clue.text: Infamous refusal to American imbibing port

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: no is a refusal
taken as written
US is short for American
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A notorious refusal to an American who has been drinking port.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious and infamous are synonyms, both meaning well known for something bad.

clue.text: Frill gets male dog upset at first

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A frilly collar makes a male dog unsettled at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' says the overturned dog comes first, before the male.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a strip of gathered or pleated fabric used as a trimming, a kind of frill.

clue.text: Highly skilled participant in a put-up job

definitions.text: Highly skilled participant in a put-up job

blocks.note: surface reading: a very expert member of a team
setter's reading: a put-up job is literally a building being put up, and the worker is skilled at height

explanation.surface: An expert accomplice takes part in a rigged scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A put-up job is a fraud, but here it is construction; 'highly' means working high up, not very.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a spiderman is a construction worker who erects the steel frames of tall buildings.

clue.text: Scholar thrown from engine into ravine

indicators.note: thrown from means ejected out of, so one piece is removed from the other

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
an engine is a machine

explanation.surface: An academic is flung from a locomotive down into a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: A chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chine is a regional British word for a steep-sided wooded cleft or gorge running down to the sea.

clue.text: A bed in Mayfair is dear, from what we hear

definitions.note: deer by sound: the answer is a kind of deer

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here within the district named

blocks.note: W1 is the London postcode for Mayfair, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
taken as written
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Lodgings in Mayfair, London's swankiest district, cost a lot, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' sounds like deer, so the definition is the deer the answer names; Mayfair's postcode is W1.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk, a species of deer, matching the sound-alike word.

clue.text: Sensational US headline has one reacting with horror

blocks.note: first meaning: American slang for a large, lurid newspaper headline
second meaning: a person who shrieks in fright

explanation.surface: A lurid American front page leaves one reader aghast.
explanation.definitionFit: In US journalism a banner headline in huge type is a screamer, and anyone who screams in terror is literally one.
